issues.legal_issue: The general acquisition statute’s award deadline does not apply to acquisitions conducted under a self-contained development scheme with its own provisions governing lapse.
material_facts: The land was acquired as part of a sanctioned scheme to develop a planned layout under a development-authority enactment.
That enactment provided its own acquisition procedure and stated when failure to execute a scheme would cause the scheme to lapse and acquisition powers to become inoperative.
The award was made after the deadline in Section 11-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended in 1984.
The development-authority enactment did not expressly adopt that later award deadline, and the scheme could operate without importing it.
issues.conclusion: Sections 6 and 11-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended in 1984, do not apply to acquisitions under the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976; the acquisition therefore did not lapse because the award was made after the Section 11-A deadline.
issues.legal_principle: The Court affirmed Khoday Distilleries Ltd. v. State of Karnataka, which construed Sections 17, 18, 27 and 36 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act alongside the Land Acquisition Act. The development-authority enactment is a special, self-contained law primarily concerned with planned development, with land acquisition incidental to that purpose; its own lapse provision governs. The later amendments to the Land Acquisition Act are not imported absent express language or necessary implication. The Court applied the principles on referential legislation and incorporation in State of M.P. v. M.V. Narasimhan and U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad v. Jainul Islam, and distinguished Mariyappa v. State of Karnataka, which concerned a different enactment that depended on the Land Acquisition Act. It also found no basis in Special Land Acquisition Officer v. P. Govindan or Land Acquisition Officer v. H. Narayanaiah to apply the later award deadline to this distinct statutory scheme.

rule.if: development_scheme_acquisition_proceeding and acquisition_is_incidental_to_planned_development and framework_is_self_contained and framework_has_its_own_lapse_conditions and not framework_adopts_general_award_deadline

predicates.development_scheme_acquisition_proceedin: The proceeding concerns acquisition of land under a development scheme administered by a development authority.
predicates.acquisition_is_incidental_to_planned_dev: The enactment principally provides for planned development, and acquiring land is incidental to that purpose.
predicates.framework_is_self_contained: The enactment provides a distinct and substantially complete procedure for the acquisition involved.
predicates.framework_has_its_own_lapse_conditions: The enactment specifies the circumstances in which failure to carry out the scheme causes it or the related acquisition powers to lapse.
predicates.framework_adopts_general_award_deadline: The enactment expressly or by necessary implication adopts the general acquisition law’s deadline for making an award.

issues.definition: When an acquisition is part of a planned-development scheme under a self-contained framework with its own lapse conditions and no adoption of the general award deadline, delay beyond that general deadline does not itself cause the acquisition to lapse.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant cannot rely on delay in making an acquisition award when the claimant’s own litigation and resulting orders materially impeded the acquisition process.
material_facts: The claimant filed a civil suit seeking a declaration that the land had not been acquired and an injunction against interference with possession.
The claimant obtained interim orders, which were confirmed at that stage in further proceedings.
The suit was later dismissed, including on the ground that the claimant was not in possession and that the civil court could not invalidate the acquisition notification.
The Court found that the litigation and prohibitory orders caused impediments to further action under the development scheme, including making the award.
issues.conclusion: The claimant’s complaint about the delay in making the award could not be accepted because the claimant had mainly contributed to that delay.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a party cannot rely on delay that the party materially caused by obtaining prohibitory orders that impeded implementation of the acquisition scheme. The holding rests on the claimant’s own contribution to the delay, rather than on a separate statutory limitation rule.

rule.if: development_scheme_acquisition_proceeding and claimant_initiated_litigation_challenging_acquisition and claimant_obtained_prohibitory_orders and those_orders_impeded_award

predicates.development_scheme_acquisition_proceedin: The proceeding concerns acquisition of land for a development scheme.
predicates.claimant_initiated_litigation_challengin: The claimant brought litigation challenging the acquisition or seeking to prevent action concerning the land.
predicates.claimant_obtained_prohibitory_orders: The claimant obtained interim or other prohibitory orders in that litigation.
predicates.those_orders_impeded_award: The orders materially obstructed further acquisition steps, including making the award.

issues.definition: When a claimant challenging an acquisition obtains orders that materially impede the award process, the claimant cannot succeed on an objection based on the resulting delay.
